```{r panel-description, echo=FALSE}
Panel G: Lateral inhibition shapes the mAL population code
============================================================
The mAL population is heavily interconnected: GABAergic subtypes inhibit
each other, structuring the population response beyond what sensory inputs
alone would predict.

Top:    mAL-to-mAL signed connectivity heatmap (rows = pre, cols = post).
```

## Build mAL-to-mAL lateral connectivity matrix

```{r lateral-matrix}
# All mAL -> mAL connections (excluding self)
mal_lateral <- conn %>%
  filter(pre_type %in% mal_subtypes, post_type %in% mal_subtypes,
         pre_type != post_type) %>%
  group_by(pre_type, post_type) %>%
  summarise(weight = sum(weight, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(
    from_nt = mal_nt[pre_type],
    signed_weight = ifelse(from_nt == "GABA", -weight, weight)
  )

# Build signed connectivity matrix
lateral_mat <- matrix(0, nrow = length(mal_subtypes), ncol = length(mal_subtypes),
                      dimnames = list(mal_subtypes, mal_subtypes))

for (i in seq_len(nrow(mal_lateral))) {
  pre  <- mal_lateral$pre_type[i]
  post <- mal_lateral$post_type[i]
  if (pre %in% mal_subtypes && post %in% mal_subtypes) {
    lateral_mat[pre, post] <- mal_lateral$signed_weight[i]
  }
}

# Filter to types with any lateral connectivity
has_lateral <- rowSums(abs(lateral_mat)) > 0 | colSums(abs(lateral_mat)) > 0
lateral_active <- mal_subtypes[has_lateral]

cat(sprintf("mAL types with lateral connections: %d / %d\n",
            length(lateral_active), length(mal_subtypes)))
cat(sprintf("Total lateral edges: %d\n", nrow(mal_lateral)))
cat(sprintf("GABAergic edges: %d (%.0f%%)\n",
            sum(mal_lateral$from_nt == "GABA"),
            100 * mean(mal_lateral$from_nt == "GABA")))
```

## Hub analysis: per-neuron lateral connectivity (input-normalized, mean +/- SE)

```{r hub-analysis, fig.width=12, fig.height=10}
# --- Per-neuron analysis using individual neuron connections from conn ---

# All individual mAL neurons
mal_neurons <- mba %>%
  filter(type %in% lateral_active) %>%
  select(bodyid, type) %>%
  distinct()
cat(sprintf("Individual mAL neurons: %d across %d types\n",
            nrow(mal_neurons), length(unique(mal_neurons$type))))

gaba_types <- names(mal_nt)[mal_nt == "GABA"]

# Total input to each individual neuron (from ALL sources, for normalization)
total_input_per_neuron <- conn %>%
  filter(post_id %in% mal_neurons$bodyid) %>%
  group_by(post_id) %>%
  summarise(total_input = sum(weight, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# All lateral mAL-mAL connections at neuron level (excluding self-type)
lateral_neuron <- conn %>%
  filter(pre_type %in% lateral_active, post_type %in% lateral_active,
         pre_type != post_type)

# --- Per-neuron INHIBITORY INPUT (fraction of each neuron's total input from GABA mAL) ---
lat_inh_input_per_neuron <- lateral_neuron %>%
  filter(pre_type %in% gaba_types) %>%
  group_by(post_id, post_type) %>%
  summarise(lat_inh_synapses = sum(weight, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(total_input_per_neuron, by = "post_id") %>%
  mutate(frac_inh_input = lat_inh_synapses / total_input)

# Include neurons with ZERO lateral input
input_per_neuron <- mal_neurons %>%
  left_join(lat_inh_input_per_neuron,
            by = c("bodyid" = "post_id", "type" = "post_type")) %>%
  mutate(frac_inh_input = replace_na(frac_inh_input, 0))

# Mean +/- SE per type
input_summary <- input_per_neuron %>%
  group_by(type) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_frac = mean(frac_inh_input),
    se_frac = sd(frac_inh_input) / sqrt(n()),
    n_neurons = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    nt = mal_nt[type],
    dimorphism = mal_dimorphism[type]
  )

# --- Per-neuron INHIBITORY OUTPUT (input-normalized: each synapse / target's total input) ---
# For each pre neuron, sum (its_synapses_to_target / target_total_input) across all mAL targets
lat_inh_output_normed <- lateral_neuron %>%
  filter(pre_type %in% gaba_types) %>%
  left_join(total_input_per_neuron, by = c("post_id")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(total_input), total_input > 0) %>%
  mutate(normed_weight = weight / total_input) %>%
  group_by(pre_id, pre_type) %>%
  summarise(total_normed_inh_output = sum(normed_weight, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Include GABAergic neurons with ZERO lateral output
gaba_neurons <- mal_neurons %>% filter(type %in% gaba_types)
output_per_neuron <- gaba_neurons %>%
  left_join(lat_inh_output_normed,
            by = c("bodyid" = "pre_id", "type" = "pre_type")) %>%
  mutate(total_normed_inh_output = replace_na(total_normed_inh_output, 0))

# Mean +/- SE per type
output_summary <- output_per_neuron %>%
  group_by(type) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_frac = mean(total_normed_inh_output),
    se_frac = sd(total_normed_inh_output) / sqrt(n()),
    n_neurons = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    nt = mal_nt[type],
    dimorphism = mal_dimorphism[type]
  )

# Also add non-GABA types with 0 output
non_gaba_active <- setdiff(lateral_active, gaba_types)
if (length(non_gaba_active) > 0) {
  output_summary <- bind_rows(
    output_summary,
    data.frame(
      type = non_gaba_active,
      mean_frac = 0, se_frac = 0,
      n_neurons = sapply(non_gaba_active, function(t) sum(mal_neurons$type == t)),
      nt = mal_nt[non_gaba_active],
      dimorphism = mal_dimorphism[non_gaba_active],
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  )
}

# Order by mean output (descending)
hub_order <- output_summary %>% arrange(desc(mean_frac)) %>% pull(type)
output_summary$type <- factor(output_summary$type, levels = hub_order)

# Store for downstream use (narrative, scatter)
hub_data <- output_summary %>%
  select(type, nt, dimorphism) %>%
  left_join(output_summary %>% select(type, total_output_inh = mean_frac), by = "type") %>%
  mutate(total_input_inh = 0)  # placeholder, updated below after type-level input

# --- Barplot: inhibitory output (mean +/- SE) ---
p_output <- ggplot(output_summary, aes(x = type, y = mean_frac, fill = nt)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = pmax(mean_frac - se_frac, 0), ymax = mean_frac + se_frac),
                width = 0.3, linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = nt_colors, name = "Neurotransmitter") +
  labs(x = NULL,
       y = "Inhibitory output to other mAL\n(mean fraction of target's input per neuron)") +
  theme_pub(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1, size = 6),
    legend.position = "top"
  )

# --- Barplot: inhibitory input (type-level, one value per type) ---
# Use adj.matrix directly: sum of input-normalized weights from GABAergic mAL types
adj_rows <- rownames(adj.matrix)
adj_cols <- colnames(adj.matrix)
input_type_level <- data.frame(
  type = lateral_active,
  total_inh_input = sapply(lateral_active, function(post) {
    gaba_pre <- intersect(gaba_types, setdiff(lateral_active, post))
    gaba_pre <- gaba_pre[gaba_pre %in% adj_rows]
    if (length(gaba_pre) > 0 && post %in% adj_cols) {
      sum(adj.matrix[gaba_pre, post])
    } else 0
  }),
  nt = mal_nt[lateral_active],
  dimorphism = mal_dimorphism[lateral_active],
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
input_type_level$type <- factor(input_type_level$type, levels = hub_order)

# Update hub_data with type-level input values
hub_data$total_input_inh <- input_type_level$total_inh_input[
  match(hub_data$type, input_type_level$type)]

p_input <- ggplot(input_type_level, aes(x = type, y = total_inh_input, fill = nt)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = nt_colors, name = "Neurotransmitter") +
  labs(x = "mAL subtype",
       y = "Inhibitory input from other mAL\n(fraction of total input)") +
  theme_pub(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1, size = 6),
    legend.position = "top"
  )

p_hub <- p_output / p_input + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a")

save_fig5_plot(p_hub, "panel_G_hub_analysis", width = 12, height = 10)
print(p_hub)

cat(sprintf("\nNeurons per type:\n"))
for (t in hub_order) {
  n <- sum(mal_neurons$type == t)
  cat(sprintf("  %s: %d neurons\n", t, n))
}
```

## Cross-group lateral targeting (by dimorphism)

```{r cross-group, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
# For each pair of dimorphism groups, sum the inhibitory lateral weight
# (only GABAergic connections = negative weights)
group_lateral <- mal_lateral %>%
  filter(from_nt == "GABA") %>%
  mutate(
    from_group = mal_dimorphism[pre_type],
    to_group   = mal_dimorphism[post_type]
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(from_group), !is.na(to_group)) %>%
  group_by(from_group, to_group) %>%
  summarise(
    total_weight = sum(weight, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_edges = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Normalize by number of possible source types in each group
group_sizes <- table(mal_dimorphism[lateral_active])
group_lateral <- group_lateral %>%
  mutate(
    from_n = as.integer(group_sizes[from_group]),
    to_n   = as.integer(group_sizes[to_group]),
    # Per-source-type average
    weight_per_source = total_weight / pmax(from_n, 1),
    interaction = paste0(from_group, " -> ", to_group),
    same_group = from_group == to_group
  )

p_cross <- ggplot(group_lateral,
                  aes(x = to_group, y = from_group,
                      fill = weight_per_source, size = n_edges)) +
  geom_point(shape = 21, stroke = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "#B2182B",
                      name = "Inhibitory weight\n(per source type)") +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(2, 12), name = "Number of\nedges") +
  labs(x = "Target group", y = "Source group (GABAergic)") +
  theme_pub(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(linewidth = 0.3, color = "grey90")
  )

save_fig5_plot(p_cross, "panel_G_cross_group_targeting", width = 10, height = 6)
print(p_cross)
```

## Lateral input vs sensory drive: does inhibition scale with activation?

```{r inhibition-vs-drive, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
# Test whether subtypes that receive strong sensory input also receive
# stronger lateral inhibition (competitive network structure)
drive_inh <- hub_data %>%
  mutate(
    total_sensory = rowSums(abs(mal_activation_matrix[type, , drop = FALSE])),
    ppk_drive = abs(mal_activation_matrix[type, "ppk23"]) +
                abs(mal_activation_matrix[type, "ppk25"])
  )

p_drive <- ggplot(drive_inh, aes(x = ppk_drive, y = total_input_inh)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = dimorphism, shape = dimorphism), size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, linewidth = 0.5, color = "grey40",
              linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_color_manual(values = dimorphism_colors, name = "Dimorphism") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("male_specific" = 16, "shared" = 17),
                     name = "Dimorphism") +
  labs(x = "ppk sensory drive (|ppk23| + |ppk25|)",
       y = "Lateral inhibitory input\n(fraction of total input)") +
  theme_pub(base_size = 10) +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

# Correlation test
if (nrow(drive_inh) > 3) {
  cor_test <- cor.test(drive_inh$ppk_drive, drive_inh$total_input_inh,
                       method = "spearman")
  cat(sprintf("Spearman correlation (ppk drive vs lateral input): rho=%.3f, p=%.4f\n",
              cor_test$estimate, cor_test$p.value))
}

save_fig5_plot(p_drive, "panel_G_inhibition_vs_drive", width = 10, height = 6)
print(p_drive)
```


## Summary statistics

```{r summary-stats}
cat("\n=== Lateral connectivity summary ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Total mAL-mAL edges: %d\n", nrow(mal_lateral)))
cat(sprintf("GABAergic (inhibitory) edges: %d (%.0f%%)\n",
            sum(mal_lateral$from_nt == "GABA"),
            100 * mean(mal_lateral$from_nt == "GABA")))

# Top lateral hubs
cat("\nTop 5 inhibitory output hubs:\n")
top_out <- hub_data %>% arrange(desc(total_output_inh)) %>% head(5)
for (i in seq_len(nrow(top_out))) {
  cat(sprintf("  %s: %.4f output, NT=%s\n",
              top_out$type[i], top_out$total_output_inh[i],
              top_out$nt[i]))
}

cat("\nTop 5 inhibitory input receivers:\n")
top_in <- hub_data %>% arrange(desc(total_input_inh)) %>% head(5)
for (i in seq_len(nrow(top_in))) {
  cat(sprintf("  %s: %.4f input, dimorphism=%s\n",
              top_in$type[i], top_in$total_input_inh[i],
              top_in$dimorphism[i]))
}
```

## Panel narrative

```{r narrative, echo=FALSE}
n_total_edges <- nrow(mal_lateral)
n_gaba_edges  <- sum(mal_lateral$from_nt == "GABA")
pct_gaba      <- 100 * n_gaba_edges / n_total_edges
n_active      <- length(lateral_active)

top3_out <- hub_data %>% arrange(desc(total_output_inh)) %>% head(3)
top3_in  <- hub_data %>% arrange(desc(total_input_inh)) %>% head(3)

# Cross-group summary
within_group_wt <- sum(group_lateral$total_weight[group_lateral$same_group])
between_group_wt <- sum(group_lateral$total_weight[!group_lateral$same_group])
total_group_wt <- within_group_wt + between_group_wt

# Correlation
cor_text <- if (exists("cor_test") && !is.null(cor_test)) {
  sprintf("rho=%.3f, p=%.4f", cor_test$estimate, cor_test$p.value)
} else {
  "not computed"
}

narrative <- sprintf(
"PANEL G: Lateral Inhibition Architecture within the mAL Population
=====================================================================

WHAT THIS PANEL SHOWS
---------------------
Top: mAL-to-mAL signed connectivity heatmap showing all lateral connections
between %d interconnected mAL subtypes. Blue = inhibitory (GABAergic source),
red = excitatory (non-GABAergic source). Rows annotated by NT and dimorphism.

Middle: Hub analysis bar charts:
  a) Inhibitory output per subtype (how much each type suppresses others)
  b) Inhibitory input per subtype (how much each type is suppressed)

Bottom:
  c) Cross-group targeting bubble plot: which dimorphism groups preferentially
     inhibit which targets.
  d) Scatter: ppk sensory drive vs lateral inhibitory input received.

KEY OBSERVATIONS
----------------
1. The mAL lateral network is %d edges, %.0f%% GABAergic (inhibitory).

2. Top inhibitory output hubs: %s.
   These subtypes are the main shapers of population dynamics.

3. Top inhibitory input receivers: %s.
   These subtypes are most suppressed by lateral inhibition.

4. Cross-group inhibition: within-group = %.0f%% vs between-group = %.0f%%
   of total GABAergic lateral weight.

5. ppk drive vs lateral inhibition: %s.

BIOLOGICAL INTERPRETATION
-------------------------
The mAL population is not a simple relay: GABAergic subtypes laterally
inhibit each other, implementing a competitive network. This competition
sharpens the population code -- subtypes with strong sensory drive
suppress competitors, amplifying the contrast between encounter types.
The cross-group targeting pattern reveals whether inhibition is primarily
within-group (competition among same dimorphism type) or between-group
(cross-dimorphism suppression).
",
n_active,
n_total_edges, pct_gaba,
paste(sprintf("%s (%.4f)", top3_out$type, top3_out$total_output_inh), collapse = ", "),
paste(sprintf("%s (%.4f)", top3_in$type, top3_in$total_input_inh), collapse = ", "),
100 * within_group_wt / max(total_group_wt, 1),
100 * between_group_wt / max(total_group_wt, 1),
cor_text
)

save_panel_narrative("panel_G", narrative)
cat(narrative)
```
